Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNDevOps

Deploys and promotions are the everyday use. Release cuts are the occasional one.

**Verify before you advise.** Every claim about this pipeline that was written down has been wrong
somewhere — `tagging.md` describes sprint tagging that is dead, `README.md:78` names the wrong MRT
target, Confluence carries three different promotion orders. `.research/DEVOPS-STATE.md` is a list
of things to re-check, **never a source of fact.** Derive state live, every time.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

---

## Modes

| Mode | Does |
|---|---|
| `status` *(default)* | Full state. A bare invocation stops here. |
| `deploy <env> <ref>` | Preflight, then dispatch on approval |
| `promote <from> <to>` | Takes what `<from>` is running and deploys it to `<to>` |
| `tag <version>` | Validates the name, checks the tag workflow is even present, cuts on approval |
| `release` | The full cut — changelog, tag, promote |
| `sync-env <env>` | `sync-env-vars-to-mrt.yml`. Prod is excluded by design. |
| `rollback <env>` | Either documented path, with the gap stated first |

**Two workflows are not dispatchable.** `deploy-dev.yml` fires only on push to `develop`.
`deploy-sit.yml` fires only on a successful `SIT Gate` `workflow_run`. If asked to deploy either,
say so and explain what actually triggers them — do not attempt a dispatch that will fail.

---

## Every invocation starts here

### 1. The ladder — what is each environment running?

```bash
for e in dev test sit uat staging prod; do
  gh api "repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=$e&per_page=1" \
    --jq 'if length==0 then "never deployed" else "\(.[0].ref) @ \(.[0].sha[:7]) — \(.[0].created_at[:10])" end'
done
```

Print all six with their age. **Flag staleness** — an environment weeks behind the one below it is
the context you would otherwise reconstruct by hand, and it changes whether a promotion is routine
or a leap.

### 2. Pipeline health

- **Environment protection rules** — `gh api repos/.../environments/<env>`. Report `protection_rules`
  and `deployment_branch_policy` honestly. As of the last check every environment returned `[]` and
  `null`, meaning no reviewer stands between a dispatch and that environment.
- **Can `SIT Gate` pass?** Does any `**/*.p0.spec.{js,ts}` exist · are `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`,
  `LHCI_TOKEN`, `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` present · is `RETAIL_APP_HOME` set anywhere the job can read.
  If not, `release/**` merges are blocked and `deploy-sit.yml` cannot fire.
- **Does the target environment have the vars this deploy needs?** `prod` has historically held
  none — its MRT vars are set by hand in the console.
- **Recent runs of the workflow about to fire** — `gh api .../workflows/<file>/runs`. A workflow
  with zero runs is about to execute for the first time. Say so.
- **Do the undeclared binaries still resolve?** `bundlesize`, `cross-env` and `@lhci/cli` are not in
  `package.json`; they arrive transitively through `@salesforce/retail-react-app`.

---

## Which ref may go where

| Tier | Accepts |
|---|---|
| `dev` | not dispatchable — auto on push to `develop` |
| `test` | a tag **or** a branch ref, for on-demand looks |
| `sit` | not dispatchable — `workflow_run` off `SIT Gate` |
| `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | **a `vX.Y.Z` tag** |

**Refuse a branch ref above `test`** unless explicitly overridden, and give the reason:
`versionGuard.mjs` skips any ref that is not a `v*` tag, so a branch ref means the downgrade guard
does not run — nothing prevents deploying something older than what is live.

Expect this to bite. **Every deployment to date has used `ref=develop`**, so the first tag-based
promotion will be the first time this rule has ever applied.

## Promotion order

`uat → staging → prod`, per `.claude/rules/tagging.md` as the Tier 1 source.

**Where a promotion also involves Contentful, say so:** `contentfulMapping.ts` and the Contentful
scripts promote content **staging before uat** — the opposite order. Both are internally consistent
and nothing explains the difference. Surface it and let Marcel decide; do not silently pick.

## The three namespaces

| Name | Where it is the truth |
|---|---|
| `prod` | GitHub Environment · `versionGuard` argument · `.env.prod` · `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` |
| `production` | `config/production.js` · `DEPLOY_TARGET` · **the MRT target** (`push:prod` → `-t production`) |
| `master` | the Contentful environment |

`README.md:78` tells a tier-1 approver to set production env vars in the MRT console under `prod`.
**The target is `production`.** Production is the one tier with no automated var sync, so this is
the only path — use the right name.

---

## Executing

Nothing runs without approval. Present, then wait.

For **irreversible** actions, print the literal command and state the consequence plainly before
asking:

- **Any tag** — *"This tag cannot be deleted or moved by anyone, including you. The `tag-rc` ruleset
  has zero bypass actors."*
- **A deploy to `prod`** — *"No environment reviewer exists. `versionGuard` will "* + (skip this ref
  / block a downgrade), whichever is true for the ref in hand.
- **Any first-ever run of a workflow** — *"`deploy-stg.yml` has never executed. This is its first run."*

Then dispatch:

```bash
gh workflow run deploy-<env>.yml -f ref=<ref>
```

Report the run URL, watch it to completion, and report the real outcome — not the dispatch's exit code.

## Tagging

Before cutting any tag:

1. **Validate the name** against both patterns — `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and
   `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`. Nothing else is accepted anywhere, and **no layer matches
   anything but lowercase `v*`** — `V0.1.0` or `0.1.0` slips past the hook, the workflow and both
   rulesets.
2. **Check `tag-validate.yml` exists on the branch being tagged.** GitHub evaluates a tag workflow
   from the tagged commit; the file has historically lived only on `develop`, so a tag cut from a
   release branch is not validated at all. Say which is true right now.
3. **Annotated only** — `git tag -a <tag> -m "<message>"`. Never lightweight. Never `npm version`;
   its commit is blocked by `release/**` protection.
4. **Push the tag alone** — `git push origin <tag>`.

## Rollback

Both paths, and state the gap before either:

> `rollback=true` skips the version downgrade guard, and no environment required reviewer exists to
> catch a mistake. Nothing else is watching this.

- **Controlled** — `gh workflow run deploy-<env>.yml -f ref=<previous-tag> -f rollback=true`
- **Emergency** — re-activate the previous MRT bundle by hand, then
  `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record <env> <ref>` so the Deployment record matches reality

## Release cut

1. `/generate-changelog` — the team's skill, and `tagging.md` says run it before cutting
2. Cut `release/vX.Y.Z` from `develop`
3. RC tags as needed, each deployed to `test`
4. Merge to `main`, bump `package.json` (Tier 1 — needs an approver)
5. Final `vX.Y.Z` tag on the merge commit — tier-1-approvers only
6. Promote `uat → staging → prod`
7. Back-merge to `develop` — required by `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, enforced by nothing

Offer `/upstream-sync-review` when the upstream watcher has flagged a new base version.

---

## When a gate is broken

**Report it, name the owner, and stop.**

Do not work around it, do not fix it, do not draft the escalation. `.github/workflows/` and
environment configuration are **Tier 1**, owned by Integration / SI Partner, routed to
`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` by `CODEOWNERS`. Not yours to change.

Give the evidence — the command, its real output, the file and line — so the report stands on its
own when Marcel takes it to whoever owns it.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never dispatch, tag, push or roll back without explicit approval.**
- **Never modify `.github/workflows/`, `config/`, `package.json`, `.claude/**` or any Tier 1 file.**
- **Never present cached state as current.** If you did not check it this run, say so.
- **Never claim a deploy succeeded from the dispatch's exit code.** Watch the run.
- **Never guess an MRT target name.** `production`, not `prod`.
- **Say what you could not verify** — MRT console state is not reachable from here, and that
  includes what production's env vars actually are.

name: SIT Gate

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  playwright-p0:
    name: Playwright P0 journeys
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium

      # Provisional: no *.p0.spec files exist anywhere in the repo yet (still early
      # development — see .docs/memory/projectState.md). --pass-with-no-tests keeps the
      # gate from permanently blocking every release branch on that basis alone, while a
      # real P0 spec that actually fails still fails the job normally — this only changes
      # the zero-tests case. The warning below keeps a "pass" from reading as real coverage —
      # scoped to match the `p0` Playwright project's own testDir/testMatch exactly
      # (playwright.config's testDir: './e2e', p0 project's testMatch: '**/*.p0.spec.{js,ts}'),
      # not just e2e/tests/zimm — a spec anywhere else under e2e/ that the project would
      # actually pick up must not trip a false "no coverage" warning.
      - name: Warn if no P0 specs exist yet
        run: |
          if ! find e2e -name '*.p0.spec.js' -o -name '*.p0.spec.ts' | grep -q .; then
            echo "::warning title=No P0 coverage::playwright-p0 passed with zero matching specs — this SIT gate is not verifying any P0 journey yet. See .claude/skills/qa-generate."
          fi

      - name: Run P0 suite
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github --pass-with-no-tests
        env:
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: playwright-report/

  deploy-playwright-report:
    name: Publish Playwright report to Pages
    needs: playwright-p0
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

  lighthouse-ci:
    name: Lighthouse CI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    env:
      LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL }}
      LHCI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TOKEN }}
      LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # SIT's MRT URL is access-controlled behind x-sfdc-access-control; see lighthouserc.js.
      # Step-scoped (not job-level) so npm install's lifecycle scripts — which inherit
      # job-level env but not this step's — never see the credential.
      - name: Run Lighthouse CI
        run: node_modules/.bin/lhci autorun
        env:
          LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL }}

      # Lighthouse records collect.settings.extraHeaders verbatim in each report's
      # configSettings — confirmed against a real run — so the access-control secret would
      # otherwise sit in plain text inside the artifact this job uploads next. Redact before
      # upload rather than trust nothing downstream ever inspects that field. Fail closed on a
      # jq error: the next step still runs on `if: always()`, so a report left unredacted by a
      # failed jq pass must not survive to be uploaded — delete it instead of uploading it as-is.
      - name: Redact secrets from Lighthouse reports before upload
        if: always()
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for f in .lighthouseci/lhr-*.json; do
            if ! jq '.configSettings.extraHeaders |= (if . then with_entries(.value = "[REDACTED]") else . end)' "$f" > "$f.tmp"; then
              rm -f "$f" "$f.tmp"
              continue
            fi
            mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
          done

      - name: Upload Lighthouse results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lighthouse-results
          path: .lighthouseci/
          retention-days: 30

  contract-tests:
    name: MuleSoft contract tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # TODO: Replace with real contract assertion once MuleSoft publishes OpenAPI specs.
      # Owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead to align.
      - name: Run contract tests
        run: npm run test:contracts

  bundle-size:
    name: Bundle size check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Build and check bundle size
        run: npm run test:max-file-size

  sit-gate:
    name: SIT Gate
    needs: [playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check all SIT signals passed
        run: |
          if [ "${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "SIT gate: one or more checks failed"
            echo "  playwright-p0:   ${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}"
            echo "  lighthouse-ci:   ${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}"
            echo "  contract-tests:  ${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}"
            echo "  bundle-size:     ${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "SIT gate: all checks passed"

content.text:
**What SIT actually is:** System Integration Testing. It's the first environment where the app runs against real connected systems end-to-end — Commerce Cloud, Contentful, MuleSoft — rather than just "does the code run" (that's what `dev`/`test` check). It sits between "code is merged" and "a human signs off" (`uat`).

**The one big split to understand: two kinds of environments**

| Type | Environments | Who triggers it |
|---|---|---|
| Auto — nobody deploys it, it just happens | `dev`, `sit` | An event (a push, a passing checklist) |
| Deliberate — someone points it at a specific build | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | A person running a command |

`dev` auto-updates on every push to `develop`. `sit` is also automatic, but with a condition attached — more on that below. This is why there's no "deploy to SIT" button for either of them.

**Where release branches fit**

`develop` is the shared trunk. **SIT never looks at `develop` directly** — it has no idea that branch exists.

To ship a sprint's work, someone cuts a **release branch** off `develop` — e.g. `release/v0.1.0` (this repo has exactly one right now, that one). That branch becomes the checkpoint for everything going into this release. Every push to it runs a checklist called **SIT Gate**: Playwright P0 tests, a Lighthouse performance check, contract tests, bundle-size check. If all four pass, SIT automatically redeploys itself to match that branch a few minutes later. The gate passing *is* the trigger — that's the entire mechanism.

**Where tags fit**

Tags (`v0.1.0-rc.1`, `v0.1.0`) aren't part of this at all. They matter one rung further up — for promoting a build to `uat`/`staging`/`prod` once it's proven. SIT doesn't use tags, ever.

**So, concretely: "we have changes in develop, we want them on SIT"**

There's no direct path — they have to travel through a release branch:

1. Get the changes onto a release branch:
   - If it's for the release already in flight (`release/v0.1.0`): branch `fix/release-v0.1.0-<name>` off it, PR back into it.
   - If it's next sprint's work and no release branch exists yet for it: someone cuts a new one off `develop` (`release/v0.2.0`).
2. **Merging that PR** — a push landing on `release/v0.1.0` — is what actually fires SIT Gate for real.
3. Gate has to fully pass (all 4 checks green).
4. Only then does SIT redeploy, automatically.

**A gotcha worth knowing as FED lead:** SIT Gate also runs on the PR itself, before merge, as a normal PR check. But I confirmed live that a PR-triggered gate run does **not** wire to a SIT deploy — only the run triggered by the actual push/merge onto `release/**` does. So "the PR's checks are green" ≠ "SIT will update." Don't take a green PR check as confirmation SIT moved — only the post-merge run counts.

**And the current reality:** step 3 is broken right now — `lighthouse-ci` is failing on the open PR into `release/v0.1.0` (#75). So even doing all of the above correctly today, SIT won't move until that's fixed. That's Tier 1 CI, owned by Integration/SI Partner — not something to route around.

The mechanism is the same either way — **a push has to land on a release branch, and that push has to pass SIT Gate.** The only real fork is *which* release branch, and that depends on what "develop's current state" actually is:

**Case A — this is new work for a release that hasn't been cut yet**

Cutting the release branch *from develop's current HEAD* is literally "take develop's state and start moving it toward SIT":

```bash
git checkout develop
git pull --ff-only
git checkout -b release/v0.2.0
git push -u origin release/v0.2.0
```

That push is what fires SIT Gate (`digital-sit.yml`'s `push: branches: [release/**]`). Nothing else to run — if the gate passes, `deploy-sit.yml` fires on its own a few minutes later.

**Case B — this is a fix that needs to land in the release already in flight (`release/v0.1.0`)**

Per our branch rules, you can't just merge `develop` wholesale into an already-cut release branch — only fixes go in, via a `fix/release-*` sub-branch, and since the change already exists as a commit on `develop`, you bring it across explicitly rather than dragging in everything else `develop` has picked up since the branch was cut:

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0
git pull --ff-only
git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-<short-name>
git cherry-pick <commit-sha-from-develop>
git push -u origin fix/release-v0.1.0-<short-name>
gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "..." --body "..."
```

Merging that PR is the push that lands on `release/v0.1.0` → fires SIT Gate → gate passes → SIT redeploys. (The PR's own pre-merge check run doesn't count, per the gotcha from before — only the post-merge one does.)

**Either way, the finish line is identical:** push on a `release/**` branch → SIT Gate runs → passes → SIT updates itself. There's no separate "now deploy" step.

Two things worth flagging before either happens for real, not just as an example:
- `release/v0.1.0` is a **supervised** branch under our rules — plan-first, confirm every edit. If we're actually doing this rather than walking through it, I'd write the plan and confirm each step with you before anything gets pushed.
- As we found earlier, SIT Gate is currently red on `release/v0.1.0` (Lighthouse CI failing on PR #75) — so today, Case B would just produce another failed gate, not a deploy, until that's fixed.

Which of the two is actually your situation — is what's in `develop` meant for the release that's already stuck trying to pass its gate, or is it fresh work for a release that hasn't been cut yet?
